Second-round independent review of the bounded correction in MIXED_READER_B_20261014/draft (task-d4de68d0fd014aba8dfbf4718d66ea83). Scope: these three draft article texts only — no opinion on MIXED_RELEASE import, runtime bundle, browser rendering, or deployment.

Corrected claim (pub-connections-011, Rear Window): I independently opened the actual Yale Film Archive PDF (web.library.yale.edu/sites/default/files/files/YFARearWindow.pdf) directly, not an excerpt. Exact program-note text: "REAR WINDOW begins with shots of the apartments while Jeff is asleep, establishing us as voyeurs on our own... Throughout, Hitchcock compels our identification with Jeff through an extensive use of point-of-view shots... With rare exceptions, we see the apartments only as they can be seen from Jeff's room." This precisely supports the revised body's qualified claim (predominant-but-not-absolute POV, opening shots during Jeff's sleep as the stated exception) and corrects the prior overstated absolute (root-editorial-finding.json's concern was valid and has been properly addressed, not just reworded). AFI Catalog page (fetched directly) independently confirms the broken-leg photographer, courtyard observation, and the telephoto-duplicating lens setup cited in the same article.

pub-connections-016: removal of the generic LOC registry link leaves AFI + Oscars.org, both fetched directly and fully supporting the body's specific claims (Lina mouthing words while Kathy sings from behind the curtain at the premiere; AFI's own framing of the piece as a silent-to-sound transition narrative). No loss of support from dropping the LOC link.

pub-connections-012: unchanged by this revision. Piano hammer-strike and harpsichord jack/plectrum-pluck mechanics confirmed via Yamaha pages (consistent with the prior reviewer's direct fetch); the specific jack-tongue-swivel/damper return detail cited to the Met PDF could not be opened by me either (10MB tool limit / 403), same limitation the writer and SOURCES.md already disclose honestly — but I independently corroborated that exact mechanism (tongue swivels past the string on key release, felt damper mutes it) via other reputable sources, so the underlying fact is not in doubt even though the specific cited Met PDF text remains unread by any reviewer. This is a disclosed, non-blocking access limitation, not a factual error, and the claim is not load-bearing (Yamaha sources alone already support the article's core comparison).

SOURCES.md footer accurately reflects the current source set (Yale PDF added/opened directly for 011, LOC removed from 016, Met PDF limitation still honestly flagged). question_refs/revision_sha256 for all three articles match mixed-runtime-bundle.json exactly.

Verdict: ACCEPT. The revised bytes correctly implement the root-editorial-finding correction with accurate, directly-verified primary-source support. v1's acceptance does not bind these revised bytes — this is an independent re-verification of the new text specifically.

Source-access limitations (for the record): the Met Bulletin PDF remains unverifiable by direct read in this session (size/403), same as previously disclosed; this does not block acceptance since the cited mechanism is independently corroborable elsewhere and is redundant to the Yamaha sources already supporting the article. All other 7 of 8 cited sources across the three articles were opened directly by me this session.

Scope reminder: this accept covers only the three draft article texts in MIXED_READER_B_20261014/draft; it is not approval of any import, runtime bundle change, browser rendering, or deployment step.
